notes: Primary source: official QSC/Q-SYS Core 8 Flex spec sheet PDF (includes rear-panel photo and full spec tables), cross-checked against Q-SYS Help hardware page (help.qsys.com/q-sys_9.3/content/Hardware/Cores/Core_8_Flex.htm) and the official Q-SYS FAQ on Euroblock connector compatibility. Unit is 1U half-width (not full-width rack), ships with rack-mounting hardware for a half-rack tray; rackUnits is given as height-equivalent. FLEX CHANNELS: 8x user-configurable analog audio channels (input or output per-channel, software-selectable), each on a 3-terminal (+/-/ground) 3.5mm Euroblock/captive-screw connector; modeled as bidirectional since direction is set in software, not fixed by hardware. Phantom power +48VDC available on inputs. GPIO INPUTS/OUTPUTS use captive screw terminal blocks (modeled as euroblock, the closest connector id); GPIO INPUTS accept 0-24V analog or contact closure, GPIO OUTPUTS are open-collector 24V/0.2A max. RS232 (COM A/COM B): spec sheet labels these "RS232" with TX/RX pins on a 3-position 3.5mm terminal connector (not a DE-9); modeled connector as euroblock (closest physical match) since no rs232-specific terminal-block id exists in the allowed list, and no grade applies (RS-232 is not a graded connector type). USB-C is spec'd as "USB 3.1" (host/device/DisplayPort-alt-mode combo port) without Gen 1/Gen 2 distinction in QSC literature; graded conservatively as usb-5g (USB 3.1 Gen 1 = 5Gbps) since QSC does not confirm Gen 2/10Gbps support — treat as a possible underestimate. USB-B and both USB-A ports are spec'd as USB 3.0 = usb-5g. DisplayPort-alt-mode over the USB-C port is not broken out as a separate DP port since it shares the single physical USB-C connector; not listed separately per the "exactly one connector id" rule for a combo port. AC input is IEC 60320 C14 inlet, universal 100-240VAC 50/60Hz, rated 1.2A per the rear-panel photo silkscreen ("100-240V~ 50/60Hz 1.2A"); modeled as connector id "iec" (C13/C14 family). LAN A/LAN B are Gigabit Ethernet (RJ45, 1000 Mbps per Q-SYS Help) — graded eth-1g; both ports are software-assignable for Q-LAN control/audio, Dante, VoIP, or redundancy, so both are bidirectional network ports, not fixed source/sink.
